logline: A corrupt detective starts seeing a righteous, motorcycle-riding alter ego who will not let him keep cutting corners - part buddy-cop thriller, part split-personality character study.

bollymeter.basis: NME gave it 4/5 and praised 'water-tight writing, pitch-perfect casting and great production value.' IMDb settled at 7.9. The split-personality premise is handled with more tonal discipline than the genre usually manages, though the back half's conventional mystery mechanics drew criticism.

pull_quotes.text: A violence-charged story that is surprisingly peppered with sentimentality.

seasons.review_body: Bad and Crazy premiered on tvN and iQIYI on December 17, 2021, co-produced by Studio Dragon. Lee Dong-wook plays a detective who is competent and deeply corrupt, comfortable with moral compromise until a second personality, K, manifests as a motorcycle-riding idealist who will not leave him alone. The series balances violence-charged momentum with unexpected sentimentality, supported by water-tight writing, pitch-perfect casting, and strong production value. Wi Ha-joon, a breakout from Squid Game Season 1, brings credibility and energy to the K role. IMDb users settle at 7.9, with a common caveat that the second half leans more into conventional mystery uncovers, following the familiar K-drama shape of a protagonist tracing back to a dark past skeleton under the original split-personality conceit. The twelve-episode run keeps the story lean enough that the formula drift lands before patience runs out.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere immediately establishes the central relationship: Lee Dong-wook's detective is smooth, careerist and cutting corners at every turn, and K appears as an interruption he cannot rationalise away. The tone - dark crime thriller with a seam of deadpan comedy running through it - is set confidently and does not overexplain the split-personality premise.
episode_reviews.the_moment: K's first full appearance on the motorcycle - the series signals it is going to lean into the absurdist premise rather than hedge around it.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 2
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The second episode sets the series in motion with the run's strongest individual IMDb rating. The detective-K dynamic moves from novelty to a genuine comic and dramatic engine. The action set-pieces deliver some of the season's most purely enjoyable sequences.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first extended sequence where the detective and K are forced to cooperate in real time - the buddy-cop formula landing before it can become familiar.
